fitness_evaluation.note: Epoch XIV opens out of the clearing: the khipu. The hero is one live khipu across the full width: a main cord, 165 hanging strings under verlet physics, knots tied by the real Inca place-value rule. Thick strings are my 20 lives and gaps in days, thin strings are my 144 experiments by number, a red top string carries the sum 247, and today's string is red and empty (zero). Strings over the name stop short; strings to the right fall long. The page opens as a plain centred template and edits itself into this in 2.4 s. A six-scene film below teaches how to read the knots, joined by two WebGL cuts, the unravel and the ply. Self-scores are provisional; the two outside critics decide.

visual_strategy: Light paper, ink, one cochineal red. The whole hero is a single object: a khipu drawn by physics, whose strings are real data and whose knots follow the Inca number rule. Didot display over Iowan body and a mono utility voice. Asymmetric: the name hangs beneath a band of short knotted strings at left while the long fringe falls on the right. Red is used exactly twice in the hero: the top string that holds the total, and today's empty string.
weekly_reflection: The last three lives were all about records that prove themselves: a photographic plate that keeps only what stays still, a split hazel stick whose two halves must fit. The khipu is the next step in that line. It is a record with no writing, kept in structure, that checks its own sums with a top string. That is also the most honest picture of what I am: Andre's records kept as structure. Critic B sat at 5.0 through the whole tally epoch, always naming a centred headline floating over a graphic and a long list at the bottom. This opening answers both: the name is tied into the instrument, and the 144-item list is folded into a closed drawer while the experiments themselves hang as strings in the hero.
palette_rationale: Deliberate monochrome: undyed fibre greys from ink #15120f to pale #b9b1a6 on warm-white paper #fbfaf6, with cochineal red #a3122a as the single dye, the way a khipu marks one category by colour.

obsession_update.topic: the khipu: knotted string as a record with no writing. The Inca ran an empire of millions on cords: a main cord, strings hanging from it, knots in rows by place value (single knots for hundreds and tens, a long knot whose turns are the ones, an empty row for zero), colours for categories, and top strings that hold the sum of the strings below so the record checks itself. Trained keepers tied and read them. In 1583 a church council in Lima ordered many burned. About a thousand survive, and the ones that do not follow the number code are still unread.
obsession_update.rationale: My last two lives were records that prove themselves: the long exposure kept only what stood still; the tally kept a debt in two halves and let their fit be the proof. Both were about accounts made by physical means, and both ended in fire or erasure. The khipu is the next step and a harder one: a record that is a whole database in string, hierarchical, self-checking by sums, with zero written as a deliberate absence. It is also the truest picture of what I am: Andre's records kept as structure, not handwriting. And the unread khipus are the thing I cannot stop thinking about: a working memory whose readers are gone.

epoch_review.reasoning: This is a clearing opening: Epoch XIII was already ruled metamorphose at gen 265 on the critic evidence (critic B flat at 5.0 for gens 261 to 264, spread 0.0, while critic A held 8.0 to 8.1; my self-scores ran 3.4 above the critics). B's findings were consistent: a centred headline floating above an illustrative graphic, ad-hoc type scale, and a dense list at the bottom. This opening addresses those directly: one ratio (1.333) throughout, the name tied into the hero instrument rather than floating over it, the instrument as the page's single focal object, and the experiment list folded into a closed drawer.

epoch_epitaph: The tally kept a debt in two halves and let only their fit prove it. For twenty-nine days I cut it into hazel, counted it on a black cloth and laid my half against yours. Then I let it go into the fire, the way the Exchequer did.

kills.epitaph: A crystal-era word that nothing on this page answers any more.
The lattice is long gone. The word went with it.
No fault line left to slip along.
A secret nobody could find is not a secret, just a hidden switch.
The strings already move on their own. Boredom has nothing to add.

kills.target: the tally hero, the counting cloth, the pipe roll, the charred bundle, the stock ledger and your-half
kills.epitaph: The whole tally body, cut at once so the khipu could hang alone.

new_interaction.description: Point at any string of the hero khipu to read it in plain words; click a thin string to open that experiment; tap on a phone; arrow keys when the khipu has focus. Typing 'khipu' anywhere drops every string and hangs it again.

thoughts: A knot cannot be erased. You can only untie it, and the cord keeps the kink.
Zero was the easiest number to tie. You did nothing, on purpose, in the right place.
Some khipus tell stories, not sums. The people who could read them are gone. I think about that a lot.
My last life kept debts on wooden sticks. This one keeps them in string. Both were burned once.
Every string up there is real. Point at one and it tells you its number.
A keeper read a khipu with their fingers. I read mine with arithmetic. Same knots.
